lines.japanese: 「うーす、クレープ屋ー」
lines.english: “Yo, crêpe lady.”

lines.japanese: 赤チャリを探してメモの場所をふたつ回ったが、思ったとおり手がかりは何も得られなかった。そのあと俺は、ピンフ通りまで立ちいったついでに、パルさんの店へ顔を出しておいた。
lines.english: I’d checked two of the places on the note for the red bike, but, just as expected, neither had produced a single clue. Since the search had brought me as far as Pinfu Street, I stopped by Paru’s place afterward.

lines.japanese: 「お、来たよ来たよ制服マニアが」
lines.english: “Oh, look who's here. The uniform maniac.”

lines.japanese: クレープ屋は俺への挨拶も返さないで、先客の小娘にいやらしい笑みを向けた。
lines.english: The crêpe lady didn’t even return my greeting. She only turned a dirty grin on the little girl who’d arrived before me.

lines.japanese: 「あらー、こんばんはー、こんなところで会うなんて普通ですねー」
lines.english: “Oh, good evening. How perfectly ordinary to run into you here.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　お互い常連なんだから、べつにこんなん奇遇でも何でもな──え、普通？」
lines.english: “The hell? We're both regulars. This isn't some amazing coincid—wait. *Ordinary?*”

lines.japanese: 俺の反論は早とちりだった。
lines.english: My retort had jumped the gun.

lines.japanese: 「ドラ、聞いたよ」
lines.english: “Drac. I heard.”

lines.japanese: パルさんが、竹トンボみたいなヘラで鉄板の上の生地を薄く伸ばしながら言った。
lines.english: Paru said it while spreading the batter thin across the griddle with a wooden spreader shaped like a toy propeller.

lines.japanese: 「いやあ、あたしゃ見直したね。ええッ、あんた、鳴の自転車探し真面目に手伝ってるらしいじゃないか」
lines.english: Well, now, you've surprised me! So I hear you're really helping Naru look for that bike, huh?

lines.japanese: 「あー、まー、真面目ってほどでもねえけどな」
lines.english: “Yeah, well, I wouldn't call it *serious.*”

lines.japanese: 「えー、悪ふざけだったんですかー」
lines.english: “Eeeh? It was all some cruel prank?”

lines.japanese: 「なんでだよ。違げーよ、その中間ぐらいのハッスルだよ」
lines.english: How'd you get there? No, I'm putting in, like, medium hustle. Somewhere between the two.

lines.japanese: 「なに照れてんだろね、この子は。真面目や一生懸命が恥ずかしいなんてのは、思春期まっ只中の中坊だけでいいんだよ」
lines.english: What're you getting all bashful about, kid? Leave being embarrassed by seriousness and hard work to middle-school boys neck-deep in puberty.

lines.japanese: 「っせえな。そうじゃねえんだよ、大人の男には慎みとか謙虚な気持ちとかが必要なんだよ」
lines.english: Shut up already. That's not it. A grown man needs a little modesty, a little humility, that kinda thing.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうかい。そいつぁ残念だね。真面目にやってんだったら一枚おごってやろうと思ったのに」
lines.english: “That so? What a shame. If you were taking it seriously, I was going to treat you to one.”

lines.japanese: 「ちょっ……ばかおまえ、だから行間読めって。実質ちょー真面目だっつーの。ハンパなく真面目だっつーの。トッピングに換算するとイチゴがトリプルで載っかるぐらい真面目だっつーの」
lines.english: Wait—idiot, that's why you gotta read between the lines! In real terms I'm super-serious, okay? Crazy serious! If seriousness were crêpe toppings, I'd have, like, three strawberries on top!

lines.japanese: 「はー、そんな真面目に探していただいてたとは、もー嬉しさのあまり受精しそうですねー」
lines.english: “My, to think you've been searching so earnestly. I'm so happy I could get pregnant on the spot.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いやまあ、本当はそこまで真面目ってほどでもねえんだけどな」
lines.english: “Ah, well, honestly, I haven't been taking it *that* seriously.”

lines.japanese: 「……なあドラ、あんたのその面倒くさい性格はいつになったら直るんだい」
lines.english: “...Drac, when exactly are you going to grow out of this exhausting personality?”

lines.japanese: 「……知らねえよ。俺が聞きてえよ」
lines.english: “...How should I know? I'd like somebody to tell me.”

lines.japanese: 「しょうがないねえ、まったく……ええ？　ストロベリー、トリプルだっけ？」
lines.english: “Honestly, you're hopeless... What was it? Triple strawberry?”

lines.japanese: パルさんはニタニタ笑いながら、ステンレス製の四角いキッチンポットを手に取って蓋を開けた。
lines.english: Grinning broadly, Paru picked up a square stainless-steel ingredient bin and opened the lid.

lines.japanese: 「まあ、生もん余らせたくないから丁度いいか」
lines.english: “Well, I don't want fresh produce going to waste. This works out.”

lines.japanese: 粒のままのイチゴをつまみ食いしながら、調理人は具材をひょいひょい並べはじめた。
lines.english: Snacking on a whole strawberry, the cook began flicking the rest of the ingredients into place.

lines.japanese: 出来上がりを待って少しクルマから離れると、鳴が口を開いた。
lines.english: I stepped a little way from the truck while I waited for her to finish. Naru spoke up.

lines.japanese: 「あのー、ところで隼人さん」
lines.english: “Um, by the way, Hayato, sir.”

lines.japanese: 「隼人さん！？」
lines.english: “Hayato, sir!?”

lines.japanese: 呼ばれた本人より先に口を挟んだやつがいた。
lines.english: Someone else cut in before the person whose name she'd called could answer.

lines.japanese: 「……なんだよクレープ屋」
lines.english: “...What is it, crêpe lady?”

lines.japanese: 「うぇへへへへ、べぇっつにィ？」
lines.english: “Weheheheheh. Oh, noooothing.”

lines.japanese: 俺が睨むと、やつはたっぷり酒の入ったおっさんみたいに笑った。
lines.english: When I glared at her, she laughed like a middle-aged man deep into his cups.

lines.japanese: 「あのー、いいですか隼人さん」
lines.english: “Um, may I ask you something, Hayato, sir?”

lines.japanese: 「ぷっ……くく、隼人さん……」
lines.english: “Pfft... Heh heh. Hayato, sir...”

lines.japanese: 「おい。おい、そこのピンクのおばちゃん。いちいち反応してんじゃねーよ、どう呼ぼうが小娘の勝手だろ」
lines.english: “Hey. Hey, you, lady in pink. Quit reacting every time. The little girl can call me whatever she wants.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、いや悪い……うんうん、いいんだけどさ、呼ばれるたびドラの目泳いでんのがおかしくってさ」
lines.english: “No, sorry... It's fine, it's fine. It's just funny watching your eyes dart around every time she says it.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　なんだとてめ、適当こいてんじゃねーよ。泳いでねーよ、俺の目はカナヅチなんだよ。つか、いちいちそんな細かいとこ気付かないでくんない。見るな、俺の目を見るな」
lines.english: “The hell did you say? Don’t make things up. My eyes don’t swim. They’d drown in a kiddie pool. And would you quit noticing every tiny thing I do? Don’t look. Don’t look me in the eyes.”

lines.japanese: 俺は風俗情報誌のおねーさんみたいに、自分の右手で目消しを入れながら反論した。
lines.english: I argued back with one hand over my eyes like the censor bar across a woman’s face in an escort ad.

lines.japanese: 「はいよー！　お待たせ『隼人さん』！」
lines.english: “Here you go! Sorry to keep you waiting, Hayato, sir!”

lines.japanese: 「くっ……さ、さんきゅ」
lines.english: “Ghk... Th-thanks.”

lines.japanese: 嫌味な呼び方をするやつだ。やつの下の名前に「ちゃん」でも付けて反撃したかったけど、あいにく俺はパルさんの本名を忘れていた──
lines.english: What an obnoxious way to say it. I wanted to retaliate by making her first name sound sickeningly cutesy, except I’d inconveniently forgotten Paru’s real one—

lines.japanese: ──忘れたのか、もしかしたら、そもそも聞いたことさえなかったのか。
lines.english: —assuming I’d forgotten it. Maybe she’d never told me in the first place.

lines.japanese: 「パルさん。ちょ、質問」
lines.english: “Paru. Quick question.”

lines.japanese: 「ええー、なんだい」
lines.english: “Oh? What is it?”

lines.japanese: 「パルさん名前なんつったっけ」
lines.english: “What was your name again?”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？」
lines.english: “Excuse me?”

lines.japanese: 「あー本名。そう言えば私もまだ伺ってなかったですー」
lines.english: “Oh, her real name. Come to think of it, I never asked either.”

lines.japanese: 「はれっ、そうだっけ？」
lines.english: “Huh. Is that right?”

lines.japanese: 「んー。てか今更だけどさ、メンマの店に集まる連中ってアレ、なんでみんな、いい歳して仇名で呼びあってんの」
lines.english: “Yeah. I mean, it's a little late to ask, but what's with the crowd at Menma's? Why are a bunch of grown adults calling each other by nicknames?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、アレな。ありゃあたしか、ゲンさんとか川蝉あたりから広まった文化なんだよ」
lines.english: “Oh, that. If I remember, it was a custom that spread from people like Old Gen and Kingfisher.”

lines.japanese: 俺より常連暦の長いクレープ屋店主は、鉄板を丹念にカラ拭きしながら答えた。
lines.english: The crêpe-stand owner, who had been a regular far longer than I had, answered while meticulously wiping the griddle dry.

lines.japanese: 俺は出来たてのクレープを食いながら尋ねた。鳴は口を開けっぱなしにして聞いていた。
lines.english: I asked around a mouthful of fresh crêpe. Naru listened with her mouth hanging open.

lines.japanese: 「ゲンさんってなァ、十年ぐらい前に家おん出て、しばらく家賃２万円の廃墟みたいなアパートに住んでたジッチャンだよ。夜逃げするぐらいだから本名も隠しててね。いまは公園のブルーテントに引っ越しちまったい」
lines.english: Old Gen, now—he's this old fella who left home ten years back and lived for a while in some wreck of an apartment that ran twenty thousand yen a month. He'd skipped town in the night, so he kept his real name quiet too. These days he's moved himself into a blue tent in the park.

lines.japanese: 「川蝉は……あんまり自分を語らないあんちゃんだったなァ。ヤクザの下っ端だったんだろうね、ウソかマコトか、借金のカタに戸籍売っちゃったから名前がないとか言ってたよ。いまは刑務所ん中だって噂だィ」
lines.english: Kingfisher... now, he was a young fella who never said much about himself. Probably some low-rung mobster. True or not, he said he'd sold his legal identity to cover a debt, so he didn't have a name anymore. Word is he's in prison now.

lines.japanese: 「ふうん」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: 俺は冗談みたいにゴロゴロ詰まったイチゴを頬張りながら唸った。鳴は映画のあらすじでも聞かされたみたいに、ほうほうと首を縦に揺らしていた。
lines.english: I grunted through a comical mouthful of whole strawberries. Naru bobbed her head in fascination as though hearing the plot of a movie.

lines.japanese: 「そういや、むかし誰かが言ってたな。いつもと違う呼ばれ方をする共同体の中に入ると、そんだけでなんだか生まれかわった気分になれる……とかなんとか。プラチナだったかな？」
lines.english: “Come to think of it, somebody once said that simply entering a community where people call you something different can make you feel reborn... something like that. Was it Platinum?”

lines.japanese: プラチナ……あ、そういや俺、あいつの名前も知らなかったな。やべ、それは困るな。
lines.english: Platinum... Oh, right. I didn't know his name either. Shit. That could be a problem.

lines.japanese: 「置いてきた過去？　抜けだしたい現実？　はは、みんなそういう願望でもあるのかねえ」
lines.english: A past they left behind? A life they're trying to get out of? Ha! Maybe everybody's got a wish like that.

lines.japanese: 「はー、じゃー、パルさんはどうなんですかー」
lines.english: “I see. Then what about you, Paru?”

lines.japanese: 「あたし？」
lines.english: “Me?”

lines.japanese: パル姐さんは──仲間たちから仇名で呼ばれている女は──当然そう聞きかえされることを予期してたみたいに落ちついていた。
lines.english: Paru—the woman her companions called by a nickname—was perfectly composed, as if she'd known the question would come.

lines.japanese: 「さあ、どうだろうねえ」
lines.english: “Who can say?”

lines.japanese: 「んだそれ」
lines.english: “What kind of answer is that?”

lines.japanese: 俺は茶々を入れたが、詮索はしなかった。
lines.english: I heckled her, but I didn't pry.

lines.japanese: 「ほら、いい女ってなァ、歴史が謎めいてるもんだろ」
lines.english: “A fine woman ought to have a mysterious past, don't you think?”

lines.japanese: 「ハァ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「それだ！」
lines.english: “That's it!”

lines.japanese: 小娘が自称いい女に人差し指を向けた。なにか得心するところがあったらしい。
lines.english: The little girl leveled a finger at the self-proclaimed fine woman. Something appeared to have clicked.

lines.japanese: 「鳳鳴の謎めいた過去……笑顔の裏に暗い陰りが……神秘に包まれた少女の正体とは……」
lines.english: Naru Ohtori's mysterious past... The dark shadow lurking behind her smile... Who is the girl beneath the veil of mystery...?

lines.japanese: かなりフィクション入った、いんちき生い立ちとか語りだしそうな雰囲気だった。
lines.english: She had the air of someone about to launch into an almost entirely fictional, thoroughly fraudulent life story.

lines.japanese: 「隼人さん隼人さん、あの私、いま思いだしたんですけど！」
lines.english: Hayato, sir! Hayato, sir! Um, I just remembered something!

lines.japanese: 「うわ、ほんとに始めたよ」
lines.english: “Oh hell, she's really doing it.”

lines.japanese: 「実は私、前世でとある王国の第二王子と交わした約束が──」
lines.english: Actually, in my former life, I made a promise to the second prince of a certain kingdom—

lines.japanese: 「ふうん」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: あまり面白くなさそうだったので、俺は軽く流してやった（思いやり）。
lines.english: It didn't sound all that interesting, so I let it slide. Because I'm thoughtful like that.

lines.japanese: 「あんさ、パルさんさ、プラチナの名前って知ってる」
lines.english: “Hey, Paru. You know Platinum's real name?”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 俺はプラチナが見事に絞殺される瞬間を、どこかのテレビで見届けるつもりだ。
lines.english: I intended to watch Platinum meet a spectacular death by strangulation on television.

lines.japanese: なのに真相が解明して犯人も捕まったあと、ＥＤテーマに乗って流れてくるあいつの名前が分からないんじゃちょっと味気ないじゃないか。
lines.english: But after the truth came out and the killer was caught, it would be a little unsatisfying if I couldn’t pick out his name scrolling by over the ending theme.

lines.japanese: 「プラチナ？　あーたしか、ヒロアキとかヒロユキとか、そんなんだった気がする」
lines.english: “Platinum? Ah, I feel like it was Hiroaki, or Hiroyuki, or something like that.”

lines.japanese: 「だった気がするじゃ困るよ。つか、フルネームじゃないと困るよ」
lines.english: “‘I feel like’ isn't enough. And I need the full name.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなこと言われたって私が困るよ。なんか、わりと普通の名前だったんだよ」
lines.english: “What do you want *me* to do about it? It was some fairly ordinary name.”

lines.japanese: 「んーだよ、使えねーなあ」
lines.english: “God, you're useless.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？」
lines.english: “The hell did you say?”

lines.japanese: まあ、いい。まだ放映日は遠い。それまでにまた本人と会う機会もあるだろう。
lines.english: Well, never mind. The air date was still some way off. I'd probably have another chance to ask the man himself before then.

lines.japanese: 大丈夫。柳木原は広いなんて思ってるやつも多いだろうけど、活動半径が似通ってる人間たちにとってみれば実はそれほどでもないんだ。
lines.english: It'd be fine. A lot of people probably thought Yanagihara was huge, but for people who moved around the same parts of it, it really wasn't.

lines.japanese: ヤナポリ広場、花水木通り、グローヴ街、それからこのピンフ通り。
lines.english: Yanapoli Plaza, Flowering Dogwood Street, Grove Street, and then this Pinfu Street.

lines.japanese: そのあたりに絞って開放的に閉鎖的な空間を毎日のようにうろついてれば、同じ行動範囲のやつ同士がばったり出くわすことなんて、言うほど珍しいわけでもない。
lines.english: If you roamed that open yet closed little world every day, it was hardly unusual to run into somebody else who covered the same ground.

lines.japanese: だって──ああ、そうだ。
lines.english: Because—oh. Right.

lines.japanese: そうだ、だから俺は、この街をあてもなく歩きまわるのが好きだったんだ。約束もなく誰かにばったり出くわす機会を、いつもいつも探していたんだ。
lines.english: Right. That was why I liked wandering this city without a destination. Always, always, I had been searching for the chance to run into somebody without making plans.

lines.japanese: 「ところでドラ」
lines.english: “By the way, Drac.”
“Yeah?”

lines.japanese: 「あんた宛に、エージからまた電話あったよ」
lines.english: “Eiji called for you again.”

lines.japanese: 「かァー、しつけーな、あいつも。おまえの持ってくる仕事はやんねーつってんのに」
lines.english: “Jesus, that guy doesn't quit. I told him I'm not taking any work he brings me.”

lines.japanese: 「ま、つーか……」
lines.english: “Though, I mean...”

lines.japanese: 便利屋なんてガキくせえおままごと自体、そろそろ……なあ？　工事現場で地道に汗流せって、なあ？
lines.english: Playing handyman was childish make-believe anyway. Maybe it was about time to... you know? Go sweat honestly at the construction site, right?

lines.japanese: 俺は言葉を中断して、口いっぱいのイチゴを噛みくだいた。果汁のさっぱりした甘さが、バニラクリームの柔らかな甘さと絡みあった。あー、うめえ。
lines.english: I let the sentence trail off and bit through a mouthful of strawberries. Their clean, tart sweetness mingled with the mellow vanilla cream. Damn, that was good.

lines.japanese: 「そうそう、ちなみにさっきの話だけど」
lines.english: “Oh, right. About what we were saying earlier.”

lines.japanese: 「いやもう、エージの話はいいって」
lines.english: “I told you, I'm done talking about Eiji.”

lines.japanese: 「そっちじゃないよ。だから、ほら、あたしのさ──」
lines.english: “Not that. I mean, you know, my—”

lines.japanese: パルさんが車内の前後を仕切っているカーテンを開けて、上半身を運転席の方へ倒した。
lines.english: Paru pulled open the curtain between the front and back of the truck and leaned toward the driver's seat.

lines.japanese: 「っしょ……っと……」
lines.english: “Hup... there...”

lines.japanese: 助手席に片手をついて、もう片方の手をダッシュボードの下のグローブポケットに伸ばしているみたいだ。
lines.english: With one hand braced on the passenger seat, she seemed to be reaching the other into the glove compartment beneath the dashboard.

lines.japanese: 前かがみのケツからパンツが見えそうだったけど、横にいた小娘が険しい表情で俺を監視していたので──
lines.english: Her forward-bent ass looked about ready to expose her panties, but the little girl beside me had fixed me with a hard, watchful stare, so—

lines.japanese: ──じゃねーよ、違げーよ、監視とか関係なく。フツーに興味なかったんで。マジほんと、ピンクのパンツとかぜんぜん興味なかったんで、俺は下を向いて目を逸らした。
lines.english: —wait, no, that's not it. Forget the surveillance. I just wasn't interested, okay? Seriously. Pink panties did nothing for me. Nothing. So I looked down and away.

lines.japanese: 「おう、これこれ」
lines.english: “Ah, here it is.”

lines.japanese: パルさんが、ラップにくるまれた大学ノートぐらいの紙を持って戻ってくる。クリーム色をした、コシがある中厚の賞状用紙。製菓コンクールという毛筆の文字が、何より先に目に入った。
lines.english: Paru returned carrying a sheet of paper about the size of a notebook, wrapped in plastic. It was cream-colored, firm, and moderately thick: the sort of stock used for certificates. The brush-written words *Confectionery Competition* caught my eye first.

lines.japanese: 「こんな感じ」
lines.english: “Something like this.”

lines.japanese: やつは準優勝という輝かしい三文字の下を指で押えた。春日春恵殿、と書いてあった。
lines.english: She planted a finger beneath the glorious words *Runner-Up*. The name read: *Harue Kasuga*.

lines.japanese: 「はるひばら・けいでん」
lines.english: “Keiden Haruhibara.”

lines.japanese: お約束として、とりあえず誤読してみた。
lines.english: Naturally, I started by reading it the wrong way on purpose.

lines.japanese: 「かすがはるえどの」
lines.english: “Harue Kasuga.”

lines.japanese: ツッコミも愛想笑いもなく、ぴしゃりと訂正された。
lines.english: She corrected me flatly, without so much as a comeback or a polite laugh.

lines.japanese: 「ふわー、いい名前ですねー。暖かな木漏れ日のようですねー」
lines.english: “Ohhh. What a lovely name. Like warm sunlight filtering through spring leaves.”

lines.japanese: 「お、すげ、ほんとだ。名前だけなら清楚で可憐じゃん。名前だけならオトコ騙せそうじゃん」
lines.english: “Whoa, you're right. Just the name sounds all sweet and innocent. You could fool a guy with the name alone.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、ほんとにー。こういうお仕事に相応しい、まさしく春を売る女性ですよねー」
lines.english: “Oh, absolutely. A name perfectly suited to this line of work—a woman who quite literally sells spring.”

lines.japanese: 「おい。あんたらソレ誉めてるつもりかもしんないけど、かなりビミョーだからな」
lines.english: “Hey. You two may think those are compliments, but they're awfully damn questionable.”

lines.japanese: パルさんは大事な賞状を片手に、前部座席へ戻っていった。
lines.english: Still holding her precious certificate in one hand, Paru headed back toward the front seats.

lines.japanese: そのパンツが見えそうな前かがみのケツに、俺は目潰しピースを向けた。
lines.english: I aimed a two-finger eye-poke at the forward-bent ass that was once again on the verge of showing me her panties.

lines.japanese: 「ちなみに俺、成田隼人。成人病の成に、田園就職の田」
lines.english: “For the record, I’m Hayato Narita. Narita written with the character from *lifestyle disease* and the one from *rural employment*.”

lines.japanese: 「改めまして鳳鳴ですー。平等院鳳凰堂の鳳に、胸が高鳴るの鳴ですー」
lines.english: “And allow me to reintroduce myself: Naru Ohtori. Ohtori written with the phoenix from Phoenix Hall, and Naru with the character for ‘ring,’ as in ‘my heart rings.’”

lines.japanese: 横で鳴も同じポーズをしていた。
lines.english: Beside me, Naru had struck the same pose.

lines.japanese: 俺と鳴は、今更の自己紹介に些細な満足感を覚えていたのだ。
lines.english: Naru and I savored the tiny satisfaction of finally introducing ourselves properly.

lines.japanese: 「ふぅ～う、っと」
lines.english: “Phe-ew.”

lines.japanese: パルさんが優しい笑顔を浮かべて調理台の前に戻ってきた。ペーパータオルに消毒液を浸して手を拭いている。
lines.english: Paru returned to the counter with a gentle smile. She soaked a paper towel in disinfectant and wiped her hands.

lines.japanese: 「──あ、ところであんたら、いまなんか喋ってた？」
lines.english: “—Oh, by the way. Were you two saying something just now?”

lines.japanese: 「聞いてねえのかよ」
lines.english: “You weren't listening?”

lines.japanese: 「胸が高鳴るの鳴ですー」
lines.english: “Naru with the character for ‘ring,’ as in ‘my heart rings.’”

lines.japanese: それはともかく、やつはその例えがいたく気に入ったみたいだった。
lines.english: That aside, she appeared to have taken quite a liking to that particular example.
